posts.title: Is Expected Utility Rational? Ecological Rationality and Ergodicity Economics
posts.description: Expected utility theory is a standard benchmark for rational decision-making, yet people systematically violate its predictions. Ecological rationality offers a context-dependent alternative, evaluating decisions in relation to their environment. Ergodicity economics complements this approach by focusing on the dynamics of the environment in which decisions are made.

posts.title: Is expected utility theory positively or normatively valid?
posts.description: Expected utility theory performs poorly as a predictive theory, while its axioms establish internal consistency rather than normative validity. Ergodicity economics provides an external criterion based on what decisions achieve through time.
